born.why: This code prioritizes survival by tightening the danger thresholds (50 for deciding, 40 for approaching) and adding a cost-benefit heuristic that rejects low-reward/high-risk items, preventing unnecessary accumulation of n1.

The code prioritizes survival by forcing a conservative choice ('a1') whenever danger (n1) exceeds a moderate threshold, and restricts approaching to very low-danger scenarios, thereby minimizing exposure to risky actions that increase n1.
The code prioritizes survival by returning the safest option ('a4') when danger is critical and 'a3' when danger is high, overriding the default choice only when safe to prevent death.

The code prioritizes survival by aggressively avoiding actions that increase the danger level (n1) significantly, using a threshold of 15 points of risk to decide whether to approach or choose a potentially safer option like 'a4', thereby extending longevity.

The existing code already prioritizes survival by checking n1 thresholds for approaching and defaulting to the known-safe option, so minimal changes are made to strictly maintain this safety-first heuristic which keeps n1 low by avoiding unnecessary risks.

The code maintains the default behavior via `x.n5` but adds a safety check to stop approaching items when danger (`n1`) exceeds 70, and avoids taking actions when danger is critical (>80) unless forced, prioritizing survival by avoiding unnecessary risks.

The code prioritizes survival by strictly limiting any single action's cost to half of the remaining safety buffer, switching to a safe default ('a4') or avoiding high-cost items entirely to prevent cumulative damage from killing the agent.

The code prioritizes survival by using a lower threshold (70) for stopping approach actions and checking pending damage (n1-n2) to detect accumulating risk, defaulting to safe behavior when danger is high or pending damage is significant.
